tools.name: search_gmail_messages
tools.description:
Searches messages in a user's Gmail account based on a query.
Returns both Message IDs and Thread IDs for each found message, along with Gmail web interface links for manual verification.
Supports pagination via page_token parameter.

query.description: The search query. Supports standard Gmail search operators.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

page_size.description: The maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 10.

page_token.description: Token for retrieving the next page of results. Use the next_page_token from a previous response.

include_headers.description:
If True, also fetch each message's metadata and include
Subject, From, and Date per result. Costs one metadata get per result,
grouped into HTTP batches of up to 10, plus retries for transient failures.
Defaults to False (output unchanged from prior versions).

tools.name: get_gmail_message_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the full content (subject, sender, recipients, body) of a specific Gmail message.

Bodies are returned inline and truncated at 20,000 characters. Set full=True to
get the complete, untruncated message instead: it is exported to disk and the
response carries a short-lived download URL (HTTP transport) or file path (stdio
transport) rather than the body, so large messages never stream through the model
context. Stateless deployments have no file storage, so there full=True returns the
untruncated body inline.

message_id.description: The unique ID of the Gmail message to retrieve.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format (only applies when format='full'). 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches the full raw MIME message and returns the base64url-decoded content.

full.description: When True, return the COMPLETE untruncated message: saved to local storage and referenced by download URL/file path instead of the body text, or inlined in the response when the server has no file storage (stateless mode). Use for messages large enough to hit the truncation limit, or when byte-exact fidelity is needed (pair with body_format='raw' for a .eml export).

format.description:
Message format. "full" (default) includes
the body and attachments, "metadata" only headers.

tools.name: get_gmail_messages_content_batch
tools.description:
Retrieves the content of multiple Gmail messages in a single batch request.
Supports up to 25 messages per batch to prevent SSL connection exhaustion.

message_ids.description: List of Gmail message IDs to retrieve (max 25 per batch).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

format.description: Message format. "full" includes body, "metadata" only headers.

body_format.description: Body output format (only applies when format='full'). 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches the full raw MIME message and returns the base64url-decoded content.

tools.name: get_gmail_attachment_content
tools.description:
Downloads an email attachment and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).
May re-fetch message metadata to resolve filename and MIME type.

message_id.description: The ID of the Gmail message containing the attachment.

attachment_id.description: The ID of the attachment to download.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

return_base64.description:
When True, includes the full attachment as a
standard base64 string in the response (in addition to any file
path or download URL). Useful for sandboxed clients that cannot
reach localhost download URLs or the MCP server's local file
paths (e.g. containerized agents with network allowlists). The
returned base64 uses the standard alphabet, so it can be passed
directly to tools like ``draft_gmail_message`` that expect
standard (not URL-safe) base64. Default False preserves the
existing behavior and response size.

attachment_index.description:
Zero-based attachment position from
the message-content response. When the cap is enabled, this lets
the server safely resolve Gmail's refreshed attachment IDs against
current metadata before downloading.

tools.name: send_gmail_message
tools.description:
Sends an email using the user's Gmail account. Supports new emails, replies, and
forwards, with optional attachments. Supports Gmail's "Send As" feature to send
from configured alias addresses.

To forward an existing message, pass forward_message_id. The original subject,
body (quoted with a "Forwarded message" header), and attachments are carried over.
In forward mode, body (if any) is prepended as a note and subject is optional.
Threading, reply, and signature options do not apply when forwarding.

THIS TOOL SENDS IMMEDIATELY AND CANNOT SCHEDULE. Gmail's REST API exposes no
send-time parameter; Schedule send is a web-UI feature with no API equivalent,
so no argument to this tool can defer delivery. Never tell a user a message
was scheduled. For "prepare now, deliver later", create a draft with
draft_gmail_message. An external scheduler must retain the message data to
create and send a new message via send_gmail_message at the chosen time, or
call users.drafts.send with the draft ID

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required for authentication.

to.description: Recipient email address. Optional when replying with reply_all=True, which derives it from the thread.

subject.description: Email subject. Required when sending; optional when forwarding (defaults to 'Fwd: <original subject>').

body.description: Email body content (plain text or HTML). Required when sending. When forwarding, this is an optional note prepended above the quoted original.

body_format.description: Format of the body content (and of the prepended note when forwarding). Use 'plain' for plaintext or 'html' for HTML content.

forward_message_id.description: Set to a Gmail message ID to forward that message instead of composing a new one. The original subject, body, and (optionally) attachments are carried over; 'body' becomes an optional note prepended to the forward.

include_forwarded_attachments.description: When forwarding, whether to include the original message's attachments. Ignored unless forward_message_id is set.

from_name.description: Optional sender display name (e.g., 'Peter Hartree'). If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.

from_email.description: Optional 'Send As' alias email address. Must be configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided, uses the authenticated user's email.

thread_id.description: Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message with an RFC Message-ID.

in_reply_to.description: Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.

references.description: Optional Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally omit when thread_id is provided; the server derives the chain through the selected reply target.

attachments.description: Optional list of attachments. Each can have: "url" (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR "path" (file path, auto-encodes), OR "content" (standard base64, not urlsafe) + "filename". Optional "mime_type". Optional "content_id" (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: ` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment. Example: [{"url": "https://host/attachments/abc-123", "filename": "report.pdf"}]

include_signature.description: Whether to append the Gmail signature from Settings > Signature when available. Defaults to true.

quote_original.description: Whether to include the message being replied to as a quoted original. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. Defaults to false.

reply_all.description: Whether to derive reply-all recipients from the thread: To = the sender being replied to, Cc = the other participants, excluding the authenticated account and from_email. Requires thread_id. Explicit to/cc win; when cc is omitted the sender being replied to is added to the derived Cc if they are not already in To. Defaults to false.

tools.name: draft_gmail_message
tools.description:
Creates a draft email in the user's Gmail account. Supports both new drafts and reply drafts with optional attachments.
Supports Gmail's "Send As" feature to draft from configured alias addresses.

SCHEDULED SEND IS NOT AVAILABLE. Gmail's REST API exposes no send-time
parameter; the Schedule send feature is web-UI only, and a message cannot be
placed in the Scheduled folder through the API. Do not claim a message was
scheduled. To deliver at a chosen time, create a draft with
draft_gmail_message. An external scheduler must retain the message data to
create and send a new message via send_gmail_message then, or call
users.drafts.send with the draft ID returned by draft_gmail_message.
Alternatively, let the user schedule the draft in the Gmail UI.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required for authentication.

body_format.description: Email body format. Use 'plain' for plaintext or 'html' for HTML content.

from_name.description: Optional sender display name (e.g., 'Peter Hartree'). If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.

from_email.description: Optional 'Send As' alias email address. Must be configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided, uses the account's default Send As address, falling back to the authenticated user's email when Gmail returns no usable Send-As entry or settings access is not authorized.

thread_id.description: Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message with an RFC Message-ID.

in_reply_to.description: Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.

references.description: Optional Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally omit when thread_id is provided; the server derives the chain through the selected reply target.

attachments.description: Optional list of attachments. Each can have: 'url' (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR 'path' (file path, auto-encodes), OR 'content' (standard base64, not urlsafe) + 'filename'. Optional 'mime_type'. Optional 'content_id' (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: ` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment.

include_signature.description: Whether to append the Gmail signature from Settings > Signature when available. Defaults to true.

quote_original.description: Whether to include the original message as a quoted reply. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. Defaults to false.

tools.name: get_gmail_thread_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the complete content of a Gmail conversation thread, including all messages.

Optionally also returns structured ownership analysis so a caller can
determine who sent the last message and who owes whom a response without
re-parsing the formatted string or making a second tool call.

thread_id.description: The unique ID of the Gmail thread to retrieve.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format. 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches each message's full raw MIME content and returns the base64url-decoded body.

include_analysis.description: When True, the return value is a dict with both the formatted thread content AND structured ownership analysis (last sender, ball-in-court verdict, per-sender message counts, participants). Defaults to False, in which case the existing string return shape is preserved.

tools.name: get_gmail_threads_content_batch
tools.description:
Retrieves the content of multiple Gmail threads in a single batch request.
Supports up to 25 threads per batch to prevent SSL connection exhaustion.

thread_ids.description: A list of Gmail thread IDs to retrieve. The function will automatically batch requests in chunks of 25.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format. 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches each message's full raw MIME content and returns the base64url-decoded body.

tools.name: list_gmail_labels
tools.description: Lists labels in the user's Gmail account.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

prefix.description:
Return only labels whose name starts with this

include_system.description:

tools.name: manage_gmail_label
tools.description: Manages Gmail labels: create, update, or delete labels.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

tools.name: list_gmail_filters
tools.description: Lists all Gmail filters configured in the user's mailbox.

tools.name: manage_gmail_filter
tools.description: Manages Gmail filters. Supports creating and deleting filters.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

filter_action.description: Filter action object (required for create). Named 'filter_action' to avoid shadowing the 'action' parameter.

filter_id.description: ID of the filter to delete (required for delete).

tools.name: modify_gmail_message_labels
tools.description:
Adds or removes labels from a Gmail message.
To archive an email, remove the INBOX label.
To delete an email, add the TRASH label.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

message_id.description: The ID of the message to modify.

add_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to add to the message.

remove_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to remove from the message.

tools.name: batch_modify_gmail_message_labels
tools.description:
Adds or removes labels from multiple Gmail messages in a single batch request.

Takes MESSAGE ids, not thread ids. Gmail's batch endpoint returns no
per-message result and silently ignores ids it does not recognise, so by
default this reads the messages back afterwards and reports which ids
actually changed.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

message_ids.description: A list of message IDs to modify.

add_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to add to the messages.

remove_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to remove from the messages.

verify.description:
Read the messages back and report per-id outcomes. Costs
one extra (batched) read per id. Set False for very large sweeps
where that cost matters and an unverified result is acceptable.

tools.name: search_drive_files
tools.description: Searches for files and folders within a user's Google Drive, including shared drives.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

query.description:
The search query string. Supports Google Drive search operators.
         NOTE: Owner-based queries ('user@example.com' in owners) DO NOT WORK in Shared Drives
         because files are owned by the shared drive itself, not individual users.
         For recent files by a specific user in Shared Drives, search by modifiedTime
         and use order_by='modifiedTime desc' instead.

page_size.description: The maximum number of files to return. Defaults to 10.

page_token.description: Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to retrieve the next page of results.

drive_id.description: ID of the shared drive to search. If None, behavior depends on `corpora` and `include_items_from_all_drives`.

include_items_from_all_drives.description: Whether shared drive items should be included in results. Defaults to True. This is effective when not specifying a `drive_id`.

corpora.description:
Bodies of items to query (e.g., 'user', 'domain', 'drive', 'allDrives').
                     If 'drive_id' is specified and 'corpora' is None, it defaults to 'drive'.
                     Otherwise, Drive API default behavior applies. Prefer 'user' or 'drive' over 'allDrives' for efficiency.

file_type.description:
Restrict results to a specific file type. Accepts a friendly
                       name ('folder', 'document'/'doc', 'spreadsheet'/'sheet',
                       'presentation'/'slides', 'form', 'drawing', 'pdf', 'shortcut',
                       'script', 'site', 'jam'/'jamboard') or any raw MIME type
                       string (e.g. 'application/pdf'). Defaults to None (all types).

detailed.description: Whether to include size, modified time, and link in results. Defaults to True.

order_by.description:
Sort order. Comma-separated list of sort keys with optional 'desc' modifier.
                      Valid keys: 'createdTime', 'folder', 'modifiedByMeTime', 'modifiedTime',
                      'name', 'name_natural', 'quotaBytesUsed', 'recency', 'sharedWithMeTime',
                      'starred', 'viewedByMeTime'. Example: 'modifiedTime desc' or 'folder,modifiedTime desc,name'.
                      Defaults to None (Drive API default ordering).

include_trashed.description:
Whether to include files in the trash. Defaults to False, matching
                    the Drive web UI and `list_drive_items`. Ignored when `query` already
                    contains its own `trashed` clause (`=` or `!=`), which always wins.

tools.name: get_drive_file_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the content of a specific Google Drive file by ID, supporting files in shared drives.

• Native Google Docs, Sheets, Slides → exported as text / CSV.
• Office files (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) → unzipped & parsed with std-lib to
  extract readable text.
• PDFs → text extracted with pypdf when possible; scanned/image-only PDFs
  fall back to a download hint.
• Images → returned as base64 with MIME metadata for multimodal clients.
• Any other file → downloaded; tries UTF-8 decode, else notes binary.

user_google_email.description: The user’s Google email address.

tools.name: get_drive_file_download_url
tools.description:
Downloads a Google Drive file and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).

For Google native files (Docs, Sheets, Slides), exports to a useful format:
- Google Docs -> PDF (default) or DOCX if export_format='docx'
- Google Sheets -> XLSX (default), PDF if export_format='pdf', or CSV if export_format='csv'
- Google Slides -> PDF (default) or PPTX if export_format='pptx'

For other files, downloads the original file format.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The Google Drive file ID to download.

export_format.description:
Optional export format for Google native files.
          Options: 'pdf', 'docx', 'xlsx', 'csv', 'pptx'.
          If not specified, uses sensible defaults (PDF for Docs/Slides, XLSX for Sheets).
          For Sheets: supports 'csv', 'pdf', or 'xlsx' (default).

tools.name: list_drive_items
tools.description:
Lists files/folders or shared drive containers, supporting shared drives.
If `drive_id` is specified, lists items within that shared drive. `folder_id` is then relative to that drive (or use drive_id as folder_id for root).
If `drive_id` is not specified, lists items from user's "My Drive" and accessible shared drives (if `include_items_from_all_drives` is True).
Set `resource_type` to "shared_drives" to list shared drive containers instead of folder contents.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

folder_id.description: The ID of the Google Drive folder. Defaults to 'root'. For a shared drive, this can be the shared drive's ID to list its root, or a folder ID within that shared drive.

page_size.description: The maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.

page_token.description: Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to retrieve the next page of results.

drive_id.description: ID of the shared drive. If provided, the listing is scoped to this drive.

include_items_from_all_drives.description: Whether items from all accessible shared drives should be included if `drive_id` is not set. Defaults to True.

corpora.description: Corpus to query ('user', 'drive', 'allDrives'). If `drive_id` is set and `corpora` is None, 'drive' is used. If None and no `drive_id`, API defaults apply.

file_type.description:
Restrict results to a specific file type. Accepts a friendly
                       name ('folder', 'document'/'doc', 'spreadsheet'/'sheet',
                       'presentation'/'slides', 'form', 'drawing', 'pdf', 'shortcut',
                       'script', 'site', 'jam'/'jamboard') or any raw MIME type
                       string (e.g. 'application/pdf'). Defaults to None (all types).

detailed.description: Whether to include size, modified time, and link in results. Defaults to True.

order_by.description:
Sort order. Comma-separated list of sort keys with optional 'desc' modifier.
                      Valid keys: 'createdTime', 'folder', 'modifiedByMeTime', 'modifiedTime',
                      'name', 'name_natural', 'quotaBytesUsed', 'recency', 'sharedWithMeTime',
                      'starred', 'viewedByMeTime'. Example: 'modifiedTime desc' or 'folder,modifiedTime desc,name'.
                      Defaults to None (Drive API default ordering).

resource_type.description:
What to list. Use "items" for folder contents or
                 "shared_drives" for shared drive containers. Defaults to "items".

query.description:
Shared drive query used only when resource_type="shared_drives",
                   e.g. "name contains 'Engineering'".

include_organizers.description:
When resource_type="shared_drives", include principals
                       with the organizer role. This costs one extra permissions.list
                       API call per shared drive returned. Defaults to False.

tools.name: create_drive_folder
tools.description: Creates a new folder in Google Drive, supporting creation within shared drives.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

folder_name.description: The name for the new folder.

parent_folder_id.description:
The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.
For shared drives, use a folder ID within that shared drive.

tools.name: create_drive_file
tools.description:
Creates a new file in Google Drive, supporting creation within shared drives.
Accepts direct text content, inline base64 bytes, or a fileUrl to fetch content from.
This stores the supplied bytes without converting them to Google Docs, Sheets, or
Slides. Use the matching import_to_google_* tool for Google-native conversion.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_name.description: The name for the new file.

content.description: If provided, the content to write to the file.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'. For shared drives, this must be a folder ID within the shared drive.

mime_type.description: The MIME type of the file. Defaults to 'text/plain'; required with return_upload_url.

fileUrl.description: If provided, fetches the file content from this URL. Supports file://, http://, and https:// protocols.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

tools.name: import_to_google_doc
tools.description:
Imports a file (Markdown, DOCX, TXT, HTML, RTF, ODT) into Google Docs format with automatic conversion.

Google Drive automatically converts the source file to native Google Docs format,
preserving formatting like headings, lists, bold, italic, etc.
Binary sources may be passed directly as base64_content. On a local server a
file on disk can also be passed by path (preferred for batch operations, so
callers do not need to load full file contents into their context).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_name.description: The name for the new Google Doc (extension will be ignored).

content.description: Text content for text-based formats. Use only for short snippets or content already in memory.

file_path.description: Local file path or file:// URL for any supported format (MD, TXT, HTML, DOCX, ODT, RTF). Appropriate for larger files than content, but file_path may still load the file into memory or perform non-streaming reads. Avoid very large files that could exceed memory or time limits; use streaming/chunked uploads or an alternative API for huge files.

file_url.description: Remote URL to fetch the file from (http/https).

source_format.description:
Source format hint ('md', 'markdown', 'docx', 'txt', 'html', 'rtf', 'odt').
                           Auto-detected from file_name extension if not provided.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.

base64_content.description: Standard base64-encoded bytes for a binary source such as DOCX or ODT.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

tools.name: import_to_google_slides
tools.description:
Imports a presentation (PPTX, PPT, ODP) into Google Slides format with automatic conversion.

Google Drive automatically converts the source presentation to native Google Slides format,
preserving slides, layouts, text, and images.
Binary sources may be passed directly as base64_content. On a local server a
file on disk can also be passed by path (preferred for batch operations, so
callers do not need to load full file contents into their context).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

and that index can be passed straight to format_text or delete_text. Tables
and multi-tab documents interleave separators, so alignment holds up to the

RECOMMENDED WORKFLOW FOR BUILDING DOCUMENTS:
=============================================
To avoid index calculation errors, build documents in phases:

PHASE 1 - INSERT ALL CONTENT (use end_of_segment=true, no index math):
  Append text, section breaks, and page breaks sequentially.
  Each operation appends to the end of the body. No index needed.

tools.name: generate_trigger_code
tools.description:
Generates Apps Script code for creating triggers.

The Apps Script API cannot create triggers directly - they must be created
from within Apps Script itself. This tool generates the code you need.
To list or remove existing triggers without opening the editor, use
`manage_script_trigger` (action="list" / action="delete") instead.

trigger_type.description:
Type of trigger. One of:
          - "time_minutes" (run every N minutes: 1, 5, 10, 15, 30)
          - "time_hours" (run every N hours: 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12)
          - "time_daily" (run daily at a specific hour: 0-23)
          - "time_weekly" (run weekly on a specific day)
          - "on_open" (simple trigger - runs when document opens)
          - "on_edit" (simple trigger - runs when user edits)
          - "on_form_submit" (runs when form is submitted)
          - "on_change" (runs when content changes)

function_name.description: The function to run when trigger fires (e.g., "sendDailyReport")

schedule.description:
Schedule details (depends on trigger_type):
      - For time_minutes: "1", "5", "10", "15", or "30"
      - For time_hours: "1", "2", "4", "6", "8", or "12"
      - For time_daily: hour as "0"-"23" (e.g., "9" for 9am)
      - For time_weekly: "MONDAY", "TUESDAY", etc.
      - For simple triggers (on_open, on_edit): not needed

editor. Neither action is read-only: the helper file may be written into the

produce the setup code, add it with `manage_script_content`, then run it with
`run_script_function`.

application_type.description: (Optional) Filter by application type (case-sensitive). Examples: 'stash' (Bitbucket Server), 'bitbucket', 'GitHub', 'githube' (GitHub Enterprise Server), 'GitLab'. If omitted, types are discovered automatically.

tools.name: jira_get_project_epic_hierarchy
tools.description:
Group a project's epics under their cross-project parent issues.

Fetches all epics in the project, detects their parent issue via
the parent field or inward issue links, then groups them by parent.
Epics with no detected parent appear under "Unlinked". Useful for
understanding how a project's epics roll up to initiatives in
another project.

max_epics.description: Maximum number of epics to fetch (1-500)

tools.name: jira_get_cross_project_dependencies
tools.description:
Find all cross-project issue links for a project.

Scans issues in the project, extracts every issue link whose
target belongs to a different project, and groups them by target
project and link type. Useful for dependency analysis across
multi-project Jira setups.

max_issues.description: Maximum issues to scan for links (1-500)

tools.name: confluence_search
tools.description: Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

limit.description: Maximum number of results (1-50)

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

tools.name: confluence_get_page
tools.description: Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID, full page URL, or tiny link. For example: '123456789', 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', or 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/x/N4CIO'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_children
tools.description: Get child pages and folders of a specific Confluence page.

parent_id.description: The ID of the parent page whose children you want to retrieve

expand.description: Fields to expand in the response (e.g., 'version', 'body.storage')

limit.description: Maximum number of child items to return (1-50)

include_content.description: Whether to include the page content in the response

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page content to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Only relevant if include_content is true.

include_folders.description: Whether to include child folders in addition to child pages

tools.name: confluence_get_space_page_tree
tools.description:
Get page hierarchy for a Confluence space as a flat list.

Returns pages with parent_id and depth attributes for token-efficient
processing. Filter by depth to focus on relevant sections, or find
pages by title. Much more efficient than rendering full ASCII trees.

Use this to understand space organization before creating/moving pages.

limit.description: Max pages to fetch

tools.name: confluence_get_comments
tools.description: Get comments for a specific Confluence page.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be parsed from URL, e.g. from 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title' -> '123456789')

tools.name: confluence_get_labels
tools.description: Get labels for Confluence content (pages, blog posts, or attachments).

page_id.description: Confluence content ID (page, blog post, or attachment). For pages: numeric ID from URL (e.g., '123456789'). For attachments: ID with 'att' prefix (e.g., 'att123456789'). Works with any Confluence content type that supports labels.

tools.name: confluence_add_label
tools.description:
Add label to Confluence content (pages, blog posts, or attachments).

Useful for:
- Categorizing attachments (e.g., 'screenshot', 'diagram', 'legal-doc')
- Tracking status (e.g., 'approved', 'needs-review', 'archived')
- Filtering content by topic or version

page_id.description: Confluence content ID to label. For pages/blogs: numeric ID (e.g., '123456789'). For attachments: ID with 'att' prefix (e.g., 'att123456789'). Use get_attachments to find attachment IDs.

name.description: Label name to add (lowercase, no spaces). Examples: 'draft', 'reviewed', 'confidential', 'v1.0'. Labels help organize and categorize content.

tools.name: confluence_create_page
tools.description: Create a new Confluence page.

space_key.description: The key of the space to create the page in (usually a short uppercase code like 'DEV', 'TEAM', or 'DOC')

content.description: The content of the page. Format depends on content_format parameter. Can be Markdown (default), wiki markup, storage format, or XHTML storage format. Either 'content' or 'content_file' must be provided, but not both.

parent_id.description: (Optional) parent page ID. If provided, this page will be created as a child of the specified page

content_format.description: (Optional) The format of the content parameter. Options: 'markdown' (default), 'wiki', 'storage', or 'xhtml'. Use 'xhtml' when providing Confluence XHTML storage format (same as 'storage'). Wiki format uses Confluence wiki markup syntax

enable_heading_anchors.description: (Optional) Whether to enable automatic heading anchor generation. Only applies when content_format is 'markdown'

include_content.description: (Optional) Whether to include page content in the response. Defaults to false since callers already have the content at create time

emoji.description: (Optional) Page title emoji (icon shown in navigation). Can be any emoji character like '📝', '🚀', '📚'. Set to null/None to remove.

content_file.description: (Optional) Absolute or relative filesystem path to read the page body from (UTF-8). Use this instead of 'content' when the body is too large to pass comfortably as a tool argument. Mutually exclusive with 'content'.

page_width.description: (Optional) Page layout width. Options: 'full-width', 'default'. Defaults to null (Confluence default).

table_layout.description: (Optional) Table width preset applied to all markdown tables. Options: 'full-width' (1800 px), 'wide' (960 px), 'default' (760 px). Only applies when content_format is 'markdown'.

subtype.description: (Optional) Confluence page subtype. Use 'live' to create a Confluence Live Doc. Only supported for Confluence Cloud.

tools.name: confluence_update_page
tools.description: Update an existing Confluence page.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to update

title.description: The new title of the page

content.description: The new content of the page. Format depends on content_format parameter and may be Markdown (default), wiki markup, storage format, or XHTML storage format. Either 'content' or 'content_file' must be provided, but not both.

is_minor_edit.description: Whether this is a minor edit

parent_id.description: Optional the new parent page ID

content_format.description: (Optional) The format of the content parameter. Options: 'markdown' (default), 'wiki', 'storage', or 'xhtml'. Use 'xhtml' when providing Confluence XHTML storage format (same as 'storage'). Wiki format uses Confluence wiki markup syntax

enable_heading_anchors.description: (Optional) Whether to enable automatic heading anchor generation. Only applies when content_format is 'markdown'

include_content.description: (Optional) Whether to include page content in the response. Defaults to false since callers already have the content at update time

emoji.description: (Optional) Page title emoji (icon shown in navigation). Can be any emoji character like '📝', '🚀', '📚'. Set to null/None to remove.

content_file.description: (Optional) Absolute or relative filesystem path to read the new page body from (UTF-8). Use this instead of 'content' when the body is too large to pass comfortably as a tool argument. Mutually exclusive with 'content'.

page_width.description: (Optional) Page layout width. Options: 'full-width', 'default'. Defaults to null (preserve existing).

table_layout.description: (Optional) Table width preset applied to all markdown tables. Options: 'full-width' (1800 px), 'wide' (960 px), 'default' (760 px). Only applies when content_format is 'markdown'.

tools.name: confluence_update_page_section
tools.description:
Update a single section of a Confluence page without affecting the rest.

Replaces only the content beneath a named heading, leaving all other
sections, macros, layouts, and Confluence-specific elements completely
intact. This avoids the data loss that occurs when a full page is
downloaded as Markdown, edited, and re-uploaded.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to update

heading_text.description: Exact text of the heading that starts the section to replace. Matching is case-sensitive. Use confluence_get_page with convert_to_markdown=false to inspect exact heading text when unsure.

new_content.description: Replacement content for the section body. Do NOT include the heading itself — only the body beneath it. Format is controlled by content_format.

content_format.description: (Optional) Format of new_content. Options: 'markdown' (default) or 'storage' (raw Confluence storage XML). Use 'storage' to insert macros or elements that markdown cannot express.

is_minor_edit.description: Whether this is a minor edit

tools.name: confluence_delete_page
tools.description: Delete an existing Confluence page.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to delete

tools.name: confluence_move_page
tools.description: Move a Confluence page to a new parent or space.

page_id.description: ID of the page to move

target_parent_id.description: Target parent page ID. If omitted with target_space_key, moves to space root.

target_space_key.description: Target space key for cross-space moves

position.description: Position: 'append' (default, move as child of target), 'above' (move before target as sibling), or 'below' (move after target as sibling)

tools.name: confluence_add_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a Confluence page.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to add a comment to

body.description: The comment content in Markdown format

tools.name: confluence_reply_to_comment
tools.description: Reply to an existing comment thread on a Confluence page.

comment_id.description: The ID of the parent comment to reply to

body.description: The reply content in Markdown format

tools.name: confluence_get_inline_comments
tools.description: Get all inline comments for a Confluence page.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to get inline comments from

tools.name: confluence_add_inline_comment
tools.description: Add an inline comment anchored to a text selection on a page.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to add the inline comment to

body.description: The comment content in Markdown format

text_selection.description: The exact text on the page to anchor the inline comment to. Must match text that exists in the page content.

text_selection_match_count.description: Total number of times the selected text appears on the page. Defaults to 1.

text_selection_match_index.description: Zero-based index of which occurrence of the text to anchor to. Defaults to 0 (first occurrence).

tools.name: confluence_search_user
tools.description: Search Confluence users using CQL (Cloud) or group member API (Server/DC).

query.description:
Search query - a CQL query string for user search. Examples of CQL:
- Basic user lookup by full name: 'user.fullname ~ "First Last"'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

limit.description: Maximum number of results (1-50)

group_name.description: Group to search within on Server/DC instances (default: 'confluence-users'). Ignored on Cloud.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_history
tools.description: Get a historical version of a specific Confluence page.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'.

version.description: The version number of the page to retrieve

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_diff
tools.description: Get a unified diff between two versions of a Confluence page.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_views
tools.description:
Get view statistics for a Confluence page.

Note: This tool is only available for Confluence Cloud. Server/Data Center
instances do not support the Analytics API.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'.

include_title.description: Whether to fetch and include the page title

tools.name: confluence_upload_attachment
tools.description:
Upload an attachment to Confluence content (page or blog post).

Provide the file either as a server-readable path ('file_path') or as
base64-encoded content ('content_base64' together with 'filename'). The
base64 form is intended for remote or containerized servers that cannot
read host file paths. Exactly one of the two must be supplied.

If the attachment already exists (same filename), a new version is created.
This is useful for:
- Attaching documents, images, or files to a page
- Updating existing attachments with new versions
- Adding supporting materials to documentation

content_id.description: The ID of the Confluence content (page or blog post) to attach the file to. Page IDs can be found in the page URL or by using the search/get_page tools. Example: '123456789'

file_path.description: Full path to the file to upload. Can be absolute (e.g., '/home/user/document.pdf' or 'C:\Users\name\file.docx') or relative to the current working directory (e.g., './uploads/document.pdf'). If a file with the same name already exists, a new version will be created. Requires the server to be able to read the path; for remote or containerized servers use 'content_base64' instead. Provide either 'file_path' or 'content_base64', not both.

content_base64.description: (Optional) Base64-encoded file content to upload directly, without the server reading from disk. Use this when the server cannot access host file paths (e.g. a remote or containerized MCP server). Requires 'filename'. Provide either 'file_path' or 'content_base64', not both.

filename.description: (Optional) Attachment filename, including extension (e.g. 'report.pdf'). Required when using 'content_base64'; it determines the attachment title and file type. Ignored when 'file_path' is used.

comment.description: (Optional) A comment describing this attachment or version. Visible in the attachment history. Example: 'Updated Q4 2024 figures'

minor_edit.description: (Optional) Whether this is a minor edit. If true, watchers are not notified. Default is false.

tools.name: confluence_upload_attachments
tools.description:
Upload multiple attachments to Confluence content in a single operation.

More efficient than calling upload_attachment multiple times. If files with the
same names exist, new versions are created automatically.

Useful for:
- Bulk uploading documentation assets (diagrams, screenshots, etc.)
- Adding multiple related files to a page at once
- Batch updating existing attachments with new versions

content_id.description: The ID of the Confluence content (page or blog post) to attach files to. Example: '123456789'. If uploading multiple files with the same names, new versions will be created automatically.

file_paths.description: Comma-separated list of file paths to upload. Can be absolute or relative paths. Examples: './file1.pdf,./file2.png' or 'C:\docs\report.docx,D:\image.jpg'. All files uploaded with same comment/minor_edit settings.

comment.description: (Optional) Comment for all uploaded attachments. Visible in version history. Example: 'Q4 2024 batch upload'

minor_edit.description: (Optional) Whether this is a minor edit. If true, watchers are not notified. Default is false.

tools.name: confluence_get_attachments
tools.description:
List all attachments for a Confluence content item (page or blog post).

Returns metadata about attachments including:
- Attachment ID, title, and file type
- File size and download URL
- Creation/modification dates
- Version information

**Important**: Confluence API returns 'application/octet-stream' as the media type
for most binary files (PNG, JPG, PDF) instead of specific types like 'image/png'.
For filtering by file type, using the 'filename' parameter is more reliable
(e.g., filename='*.png' pattern matching if supported, or exact filename).

Useful for:
- Discovering what files are attached to a page
- Getting attachment IDs for download operations
- Checking if a specific file exists
- Listing images/documents for processing

content_id.description: The ID of the Confluence content (page or blog post) to list attachments for. Example: '123456789'

start.description: (Optional) Starting index for pagination. Use 0 for the first page. To get the next page, add the 'limit' value to 'start'. Default: 0

limit.description: (Optional) Maximum number of attachments to return per request (1-100). Use pagination (start/limit) for large attachment lists. Default: 50

filename.description: (Optional) Filter results to only attachments matching this filename. Exact match only. Example: 'report.pdf'

media_type.description: (Optional) Filter by MIME type. **Note**: Confluence API returns 'application/octet-stream' for most binary files (PNG, JPG, PDF) instead of specific MIME types like 'image/png'. For more reliable filtering, use the 'filename' parameter. Examples: 'application/octet-stream' (binary files), 'application/pdf', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document' (for .docx)

tools.name: confluence_download_attachment
tools.description:
Download an attachment from Confluence as an embedded resource.

Returns the attachment content as a base64-encoded embedded resource so
that it is available over the MCP protocol without requiring filesystem
access on the server. Files larger than 50 MB are not downloaded inline;
a descriptive error message is returned instead.

attachment_id.description: The ID of the attachment to download (e.g., 'att123456789'). Find attachment IDs using get_attachments tool. Example workflow: get_attachments(content_id) → use returned ID here.

tools.name: confluence_download_content_attachments
tools.description:
Download all attachments for a Confluence content item as embedded resources.

Returns attachment contents as base64-encoded embedded resources so that
they are available over the MCP protocol without requiring filesystem
access on the server. Files larger than 50 MB are skipped with an error
entry in the summary.

content_id.description: The ID of the Confluence content (page or blog post) to download attachments from. Example: '123456789'

tools.name: confluence_delete_attachment
tools.description:
Permanently delete an attachment from Confluence.

**Warning**: This action cannot be undone! The attachment and ALL its versions will be
permanently deleted.

Use this tool to:
- Remove outdated or incorrect attachments
- Clean up duplicate files
- Delete sensitive information that was accidentally uploaded

Best practices:
- Verify the attachment ID before deletion using get_attachments
- Consider downloading the attachment first as a backup
- Check with content owners before deleting shared attachments

attachment_id.description: The ID of the attachment to delete. Attachment IDs can be found using the get_attachments tool. Example: 'att123456789'. **Warning**: This permanently deletes the attachment and all its versions.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_images
tools.description:
Get all images attached to a Confluence page as inline image content.

Filters attachments to images only (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG, BMP)
and returns them as base64-encoded ImageContent that clients can
render directly. Non-image attachments are excluded.

Files with ambiguous MIME types (application/octet-stream) are
detected by filename extension as a fallback. Images larger than
50 MB are skipped with an error entry in the summary.

content_id.description: The ID of the Confluence page or blog post to retrieve images from. Example: '123456789'

tools.name: confluence_list_page_templates
tools.description:
List Confluence page content templates.

This operation is only available for Confluence Cloud.
Returns template metadata (ID, name, description, type) without the
full body.  Use confluence_get_page_template to fetch a template's body.

space_key.description: Optional space key to list templates defined in that space. When omitted, global templates are returned.

limit.description: Maximum number of templates to return.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_template
tools.description: Get a Cloud page template by ID, including its storage-format body.

template_id.description: The ID of the template to retrieve.

tools.name: confluence_create_page_from_template
tools.description:
Create a new Cloud page pre-populated with a template's body.

This operation is only available for Confluence Cloud.
Fetches the named template and creates a page with its storage-format
content.  The page can be edited afterwards via confluence_update_page.

space_key.description: Key of the space in which to create the page.

template_id.description: ID of the template to use as the page body.

parent_id.description: Optional ID of the parent page.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_restrictions
tools.description:
Get view and edit restrictions for a Confluence page.

Returns the current restriction lists for the read (view) and update (edit)
operations.  An empty list means the page is unrestricted for that operation.

tools.name: confluence_set_page_restrictions
tools.description:
Set view and edit restrictions on a Confluence page.

Replaces all existing restrictions with the provided lists.  Omitting all
parameters (or passing empty lists) removes all restrictions.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to restrict

read_users.description: (Optional) Account IDs (Cloud) or usernames (Server/DC) allowed to view the page. Empty list = unrestricted.

read_groups.description: (Optional) Group names allowed to view the page.

edit_users.description: (Optional) Account IDs (Cloud) or usernames (Server/DC) allowed to edit the page.

edit_groups.description: (Optional) Group names allowed to edit the page.

tools.name: confluence_copy_page
tools.description:
Copy a Confluence page to a new location.

On Confluence Cloud the native copy endpoint is used.  On Server/Data Center
the page body is fetched and a new page is created manually (attachments are
not copied in the Server/DC path).

source_page_id.description: The ID of the page to copy

destination_space_key.description: Space key for the new page (e.g. 'DEV', 'TEAM')

new_title.description: Title for the new copied page

destination_parent_id.description: (Optional) Parent page ID in the destination space. When omitted the page is created at the space root.

copy_attachments.description: (Optional) Whether to copy attachments to the new page. Defaults to true. Only supported on Confluence Cloud.

tools.name: confluence_check_content_permissions
tools.description:
Check whether a user or group can perform an operation on specific content.

Wraps POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/permission/check.

Note: This tool is only available for Confluence Cloud. Server/Data Center
instances use different permission APIs.

Returns a JSON object with a 'hasPermission' boolean indicating whether
the subject has the requested permission on the content.

content_id.description: Confluence content ID (page, blog post, comment, or attachment). Example: '123456789'

user_identifier.description: Account ID of the user (for subject_type='user') or group ID (for subject_type='group'). Example user account ID: '5b10a2844c20165700ede21g'

operation.description: The operation to check. Common values: 'read', 'update', 'delete', 'export', 'purge', 'administer', 'create_or_delete_from_view'.

subject_type.description: Whether the subject is a 'user' or a 'group'. Defaults to 'user'.

tools.name: confluence_get_space_permissions
tools.description:
List all permission assignments for a Confluence space.

Wraps GET /wiki/api/v2/spaces/{id}/permissions.

Note: This tool is only available for Confluence Cloud. Server/Data Center
instances use different permission APIs.

Returns a JSON object with a 'results' list of permission assignment objects.
Each entry contains the principal (user or group), the operation permitted,
and the target. Use this to audit who has access to a space.

space_id.description: Numeric ID of the Confluence space. This is the internal space ID, not the space key. Example: '98304'. You can find the space ID from the Confluence REST API (GET /wiki/api/v2/spaces) or from the space URL.

limit.description: Maximum number of permission entries to return. Defaults to 25.

cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor from a previous response.
